amendments.stage: after the test-set runs (benchmark calibration, 6 draws) were read
amendments.deviation: The registration named p_fin (the calibrated rank of the cross-fitted statistic sigma) as the method's output and the fold-pooled sigma as a diagnostic. On the test sets, p_fin x TINS is worse than the Phase 12 read-out x TINS by 3.00 [2.90, 3.10] FPR95 points on near-OOD (13.25 vs 10.26) and worse than p_fin alone (11.52), while sigma x TINS is 10.50 (+0.24 [0.13, 0.35] vs the Phase 12 read-out) and sigma alone 11.50 (p_fin alone 11.52). Cause: p_fin is a rank with floor 1/(n_b+1); every image whose sigma is below the smallest calibration sigma (most of the unknowns) gets the same minimum, so the base detector's log-score decides their order and the near-OOD weakness of TINS enters the product. sigma has no floor. The same ordering was already visible on dev1 (sigma|TINS 13.80 < v1|TINS 14.34 < p_fin|TINS 14.99), but the registration did not foresee it.
amendments.change: The score used for AUROC/FPR95 in every table is s = s0 * exp(sigma) (sigma = sum over views of log p+~ + log p-~, cross-fitted); p_fin = calibrated rank of sigma remains the decision output and the object of Proposition 4 and of all validity checks. Standalone, sigma and p_fin give the same ranking up to the fold pooling (11.50 vs 11.52 near, 5.17 vs 5.15 far, 4.56 vs 4.55 Four-OOD). The registered-form rows (p_fin standalone and p_fin x TINS) are reported in the ablation table and this deviation is stated in the paper.
amendments.not_changed: the selected configuration (storey, q = 0.2, pp), the views, k_g, lambda, the fold split, the base detector, every data set and draw
